To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The SAGE algorithm is able to track the fast fading channels in the amplify-and-forward relays, and that the resulting error performance can approach the error performance of a non-fading channel.

the SAGE algorithm can be used to perform iterative channel estimation from signals in an Amplified-and-Forward protocol and that the error performance of a cooperative system with channel estimation is better than the error performance of the same system with perfect channel state information at the receiver.
the SAGE algorithm provides a fast and accurate solution for the channel estimation problem in amplify-and-forward relays.
In summary, our research is concerned with

1) the development of a maximum-likelihood channel estimator, based on the SAGE algorithm, for the Amplify-and- Forward protocol, 2) the investigation of the effect of the channel estimation errors on the error performance and 3) the investigation of how to improve the performance of the channel estimator by using a-priori information.
the following questions: (i) How does channel estimation affect the performance of cooperative communication?
the following questions: 1) What is the performance of the iterative SAGE-based channel estimation algorithm?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed SAGE algorithm is able to estimate the channels to a high accuracy, even when the SNR is relatively low.
, in a cooperative system, the SAGE channel estimation algorithm performs very well in terms of error performance, especially in the case of low SNR.
SAGE performs well in the case of low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), while the maximum-likelihood (ML) approach performs better at high SNRs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show the performance gain of the SAGE algorithm compared with the least-squares channel estimation, and the importance of channel estimation for error performance.

, in the absence of channel state information at the receiver, the SAGE-based channel estimation technique is capable of providing the receiver with a good estimate of the channel, and that, with this channel estimate, the error performance of the cooperative system is comparable to the case where perfect channel state information is known.

we propose a maximum-likelihood channel estimation algorithm that can be implemented in a practical way, and that we show that the resulting error performance is very close to that of the ideal scenario where all channel state information (CSI) is available at the receiver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of a single relay node, iterative estimation is not necessary to achieve the same performance as if the channel was known perfectly.

the performance of cooperative communication is significantly affected by the channel estimation error, and the SAGE algorithm can provide a significant performance gain compared to the non-iterative channel estimation scheme.

channel estimation and decoding can be performed in parallel and with low complexity, and that the resulting performance is close to that of a scheme where perfect channel information is available at both the source and the destination.
